title: Morning Edition
notes: Leading this morning: Xi Jinping’s airport welcome for Donald Trump in Shenzhen ahead of Thursday’s planned three-way summit with Vladimir Putin, Mary Peltola’s Senate win in Alaska, Canada–U.S. trade talks, Hong Kong’s Ngau Tam Mei funding request, Xi’s free-trade pitch at APEC and the EU’s €45 billion plan for Ukraine. Culture, sport and everyday-life stories include Grand Theft Auto VI, Oprah’s Canadian book pick, the Edmonton Elks’ Grey Cup celebration, Canada’s alert test and later school start times in China.

Updates on earlier stories: Nvidia’s results (Tuesday’s edition said they were due), the U.S. measles status (first reported Nov 14 from unnamed sources, now announced by PAHO), the CUHK Medical Centre surgical error (first reported Tuesday) and the Elks’ Grey Cup (previewed Nov 15).

Still planned, not yet happened when this edition was prepared: the Xi–Trump–Putin meeting and APEC leaders’ talks in Shenzhen, Canada’s Alert Ready test, the release of Grand Theft Auto VI and EU governments’ decision on the Ukraine loan.

Photos appear on the lead and on 18 of 24 other stories; all are file photos credited and licensed as shown. Text-only: Grand Theft Auto VI, Jorge Linares, the Alert Ready test, Oprah’s book pick, the Hong Kong–Chile working holiday scheme and DeepSeek, where no suitable openly licensed photo was found.
Stories by region: U.S. 5, Canada 5, Hong Kong 5, China 5, World 5. Several stories rest on a single outlet; this is noted under each story’s sources.
provenance: Compiled from the linked reporting, official releases and state-media reports listed under each story; labels show whether a point is reported, an official statement, a claim, an allegation or analysis.
Source pages were opened during this morning’s research between about 6:17 AM and 6:19 AM ET; each check time is the logged time that page was fetched.

RTHK is Hong Kong’s government-funded broadcaster; info.gov.hk is the Hong Kong government’s press-release site; Xinhua is Chinese state media; Sixth Tone is owned by a state-owned Shanghai media group. Wire copy carried by another outlet is marked with the agency’s name.

The South China Morning Post and ESPN did not return article text to automated fetches this morning (HTTP 403 and a bot check); those are access limits, not evidence of errors, and they are not cited.

stories.headline: Xi greets Trump on the tarmac in Shenzhen, a day before their planned three-way summit with Putin
stories.deck: Xi Jinping met Donald Trump at the foot of Air Force One in Shenzhen on Wednesday afternoon local time, hours after holding talks with Vladimir Putin. The first meeting of the three leaders is scheduled for Thursday, Nov. 19, on the sidelines of the APEC summit.
stories.summary: Xi Jinping met Donald Trump at the foot of Air Force One in Shenzhen on Wednesday afternoon local time, hours after holding talks with Vladimir Putin. The first meeting of the three leaders is scheduled for Thursday, Nov. 19, on the sidelines of the APEC summit. NPR said the leaders’ handshake turned into a hug as dancers waved flowers and flags, returning a gesture Trump made during Xi’s state visit to Washington in September; Xi did not meet Putin at the airport when he arrived earlier on Wednesday. According to Xinhua, as quoted by DW and RTHK, Xi told Trump he looked forward to an “in-depth exchange of views” aimed at “a constructive, strategically stable relationship.” Trump has said he plans to raise limits on nuclear weapons and an end to the war in Ukraine at Thursday’s meeting; RTHK, citing agencies, said the wars in Iran and Ukraine were expected on the agenda. Secretary of State Marco Rubio, travelling with Trump, said there was “zero” evidence that a string of recent U.S. technology outages was linked to rival countries or hackers, NPR reported. Analysts quoted by Al Jazeera and NPR expect few concrete agreements; DW noted the U.S.–China tariff truce currently runs only until early January.
stories.why: This is the first time the leaders of the three biggest nuclear powers will sit down together, and what they say about Ukraine, Iran and arms control will be read in every capital. For trade, the clock matters most: the truce that keeps U.S.–China tariffs down expires in early January, so any sign of an extension or a deeper deal would affect prices and supply chains far beyond the two countries.
stories.label: Reported + Official statement + State media

stories.headline: Democrat Mary Peltola wins Alaska’s Senate race, expanding her party’s Senate majority to 56–44
stories.deck: Peltola defeated Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan after two weeks of counting, settling the last Senate race of the Nov. 3 midterms. Democrats flipped nine Republican-held seats, the most since 1958, according to AP reporting carried by CBC.
stories.summary: Peltola defeated Republican Sen. Dan Sullivan after two weeks of counting, settling the last Senate race of the Nov. 3 midterms. Democrats flipped nine Republican-held seats, the most since 1958, according to AP reporting carried by CBC. DW, citing the AP call, said Peltola crossed 50% of first-choice votes, with 144,302 to Sullivan’s 131,844. The BBC said she is the first Alaska Native elected to the Senate and the first Democrat to win a Senate seat in Alaska since 2008. The race was overshadowed by a New York Times report that people working with her campaign tried to recruit a candidate also named Dan Sullivan to split the vote; Peltola denied any involvement, and Trump called for her prosecution, CBC reported. The BBC said Sullivan had not yet commented. Democrats also won back the House.
stories.why: With both chambers in Democratic hands for Trump’s last two years, his legislative agenda will need Democratic votes and Congress gains new power to investigate the administration. A wider Senate margin also gives Democrats room on confirmations.
stories.label: Reported + Allegation

stories.headline: Nvidia’s board rules out bringing back Jensen Huang as quarterly sales double to $115.8 billion
stories.deck: In its first results since Huang’s resignation, Nvidia reported sales of $115.8 billion for the three months to Oct. 25. Chair Harvey Jones said the board “does not intend to reinstate” Huang, hours after Huang said he would be honoured to return, the BBC reported.
stories.summary: In its first results since Huang’s resignation, Nvidia reported sales of $115.8 billion for the three months to Oct. 25. Chair Harvey Jones said the board “does not intend to reinstate” Huang, hours after Huang said he would be honoured to return, the BBC reported. Profit doubled from a year earlier to $65 billion and data-centre sales doubled to $107 billion; the company forecast another 13% rise in revenue next quarter, and its shares rose 4.8% after hours. Interim chief executive Colette Kress said it was “business as usual.” DW reported that Kress also said Nvidia is no longer shipping licensed Hopper data-centre chips to China, after selling $2.4 billion of them the previous quarter; she did not say why. Huang, who co-founded the company, resigned last week after reports of extramarital affairs, including one with a woman U.S. officials suspect is a Chinese intelligence asset; China denies the spying claims.
stories.why: Nvidia’s chips power most of the AI boom, so its numbers move markets well beyond tech. The end of Hopper shipments to China, disclosed as Trump meets Xi, is a concrete sign of how the spy scandal is reshaping U.S.–China chip trade.
stories.label: Company figures + Reported + Allegation
stories.note: Tuesday’s edition said the results were due; this is the outcome.

stories.headline: The U.S. loses its measles elimination status after 26 years, the Pan American Health Organization says
stories.deck: PAHO said on Tuesday that the same measles strain has circulated in the U.S. without interruption for more than 12 months, ending the elimination status the country has held since 2000. Mexico and Bolivia also lost their status, the BBC reported.
stories.summary: PAHO said on Tuesday that the same measles strain has circulated in the U.S. without interruption for more than 12 months, ending the elimination status the country has held since 2000. Mexico and Bolivia also lost their status, the BBC reported. PAHO director Jarbas Barbosa blamed persistent “gaps in vaccination” and called it “a serious warning for our region, but it is not an irreversible setback.” The CDC said it was committed to regaining the status by expanding access to vaccines. DW said the CDC had confirmed 5,412 cases and six deaths this year as of Nov. 12, while states have reported 10 deaths; Pennsylvania has been hardest hit, with seven deaths and more than 1,500 cases. Two doses of the MMR vaccine are 97% effective, the BBC noted.
stories.why: The designation is largely symbolic, but it confirms that measles is circulating continuously again in the U.S. Anyone who spends time in crowded places such as dorms or public transit may want to check they have had both MMR doses.
stories.label: Official statement + Reported
stories.note: The Nov 14 edition reported the expected decision, citing people familiar with it; this is PAHO’s announcement.

stories.headline: Grand Theft Auto VI is due out Thursday after 13 years, and NPR’s critic calls it “a gaming triumph”
stories.deck: Rockstar Games’ first new Grand Theft Auto since 2013 is set for release at midnight on Thursday, the BBC reports. NPR’s review, published Wednesday, calls it “a grounded love story, a gonzo crime thriller and a gaming triumph.”
stories.summary: Rockstar Games’ first new Grand Theft Auto since 2013 is set for release at midnight on Thursday, the BBC reports. NPR’s review, published Wednesday, calls it “a grounded love story, a gonzo crime thriller and a gaming triumph.” The game is set in Leonida, a fictional take on Florida, and follows the pair Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval around Vice City. NPR’s critic describes it as part Bonnie and Clyde love story and part satire of American culture, and notes changes that slow the usual mayhem, such as storing guns in a car’s trunk. The BBC said fans have booked days off and bought new consoles for launch; market-intelligence firm Sensor Tower estimates 12 million pre-orders worth $1.18 billion, a figure Rockstar has not confirmed.
stories.why: GTA VI is expected to be one of the biggest entertainment launches ever, bigger than most film openings. Its reception will set the tone for games as a storytelling medium — and the performance-capture acting that drives it.

stories.headline: Former world boxing champion Jorge Linares is held by ICE in Texas and faces deportation proceedings
stories.deck: The 41-year-old Venezuelan, a three-weight world champion, was detained at El Paso International Airport on Sunday and remains in custody pending removal proceedings, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement said on Tuesday.
stories.summary: The 41-year-old Venezuelan, a three-weight world champion, was detained at El Paso International Airport on Sunday and remains in custody pending removal proceedings, U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement said on Tuesday. An ICE spokesperson told the BBC that Linares entered the U.S. in October 2023 with permission to stay temporarily and overstayed, adding that “a pending application or work authorisation does not confer legal status.” His lawyers, Wilner & O’Reilly, said he “is authorised to be in the United States” and has cooperated fully. Al Jazeera confirmed through ICE’s online detainee locator that he is held at the El Paso Processing Center. Linares, who is based in Miami, posted on Sunday: “ICE has detained me in El Paso, Texas. This is crazy.”
stories.why: Linares is one of the best-known athletes caught up in the administration’s stepped-up immigration enforcement. His case tests whether pending applications protect people who entered legally, a question facing many visa holders.
stories.label: Official statement + Claim + Reported

stories.headline: Canada–U.S. trade talks are picking up again with weekly calls, CBC reports citing senior officials
stories.deck: Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc has been meeting U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick weekly by phone and video since talks restarted earlier this month, three senior government officials told CBC News. There is no formal deal on the table, they said, and auto and steel tariffs remain key sticking points.
stories.summary: Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc has been meeting U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick weekly by phone and video since talks restarted earlier this month, three senior government officials told CBC News. There is no formal deal on the table, they said, and auto and steel tariffs remain key sticking points. Chief negotiator Janice Charette usually joins the calls, and there are no plans for LeBlanc to travel to Washington, unlike the summer, when talks collapsed and the U.S. added tariffs. Prime Minister Mark Carney said on Nov. 1 that the teams would start working again. Speaking to a Commons committee on Tuesday, LeBlanc said, in French, that a deal was possible that serves Canada, the U.S. “and ultimately also our Mexican partners.” The federal advisory committee on Canada–U.S. relations is scheduled to meet virtually on Thursday, its first meeting since the midterms.
stories.why: Auto and steel tariffs weigh heavily on factory towns, especially in Ontario, so any movement matters for jobs. Ottawa is also widening its trade deal with China at the same time, a balancing act Washington is watching.

stories.headline: Ottawa writes off about $4.5 billion in COVID-19 benefit debts it says it cannot collect
stories.deck: The federal government wrote off about $4.5 billion owed by people who received pandemic benefits they were later deemed ineligible for, the Auditor General highlighted last week, CBC News reports. That is up from $26 million in write-offs the previous year.
stories.summary: The federal government wrote off about $4.5 billion owed by people who received pandemic benefits they were later deemed ineligible for, the Auditor General highlighted last week, CBC News reports. That is up from $26 million in write-offs the previous year. The write-offs were recorded as “uncollectable” in the 2025–26 fiscal year, which ended March 31. Employment and Social Development Canada told CBC that most of them “pertained to deceased or vulnerable populations.” The Canada Revenue Agency estimates it paid about $14 billion in COVID-19 benefits to people who did not meet income requirements; the amount still owed fell to about $5.56 billion by the end of July, partly because of eligibility changes and write-offs.
stories.why: The write-off is a large sum for taxpayers, but it also ends years of uncertainty for many low-income people who were told to repay benefits they received in good faith. Expect it to feed the debate over how emergency aid should be designed next time.

stories.headline: Canada’s Alert Ready system is scheduled to sound a test alert on phones, TV and radio on Wednesday, Nov. 18
stories.deck: The National Public Alerting System plans to test its Alert Ready emergency alerts in every province and territory on Wednesday, CBC News reports. The test is scheduled for 12:55 p.m. in Ontario and 1:55 p.m. local time in most other provinces.
stories.summary: The National Public Alerting System plans to test its Alert Ready emergency alerts in every province and territory on Wednesday, CBC News reports. The test is scheduled for 12:55 p.m. in Ontario and 1:55 p.m. local time in most other provinces; New Brunswick’s is at 10:55 a.m. and Newfoundland and Labrador’s at 9:55 a.m. It will reach TV, radio and compatible phones on LTE or 5G networks, starting with the distinctive tone and a message saying it is a test and no action is needed. Canadians cannot opt out, said Pelmorex, which runs the system’s technical side. The system has sent more than 1,215 real alerts across Canada so far this year.
stories.why: The test checks that warnings for wildfires, floods, tornadoes and Amber alerts actually reach people. If your phone stays silent, it is worth checking its emergency-alert settings and network.

stories.headline: Edmonton Elks fans celebrate the club’s first Grey Cup since 2015
stories.deck: Thousands of fans in green and gold packed the Edmonton Expo Centre on Tuesday evening to celebrate the Elks’ 37–30 win over the Montreal Alouettes in Sunday’s 113th Grey Cup in Calgary, CBC News reports.
stories.summary: Thousands of fans in green and gold packed the Edmonton Expo Centre on Tuesday evening to celebrate the Elks’ 37–30 win over the Montreal Alouettes in Sunday’s 113th Grey Cup in Calgary, CBC News reports. Players held up a “City of Champions” sign. It is the club’s 15th championship and its first in 11 years, and it came after the team ended a seven-year playoff drought earlier this month. Owner Deb Thompson, who took over after her husband Larry Thompson died last year, thanked fans: “You stuck with us through some tough years.”
stories.why: After a seven-year playoff drought and several difficult seasons, the title is a lift for a city that turns out for its football team, and a reminder of the CFL’s regional pull.

stories.headline: CUHK Medical Centre says the doctor who removed a patient’s ovaries by mistake “zoned out”
stories.deck: The private hospital’s chief executive, Chung Kin-lai, apologised at a press conference on Wednesday and said the doctor was “absent-minded or zoned out” and carried out the option the patient had not chosen during a September operation, RTHK reports.
stories.summary: The private hospital’s chief executive, Chung Kin-lai, apologised at a press conference on Wednesday and said the doctor was “absent-minded or zoned out” and carried out the option the patient had not chosen during a September operation, RTHK reports. The patient had chosen to keep her ovaries during a laparoscopic hysterectomy. A day earlier, the hospital said the doctor had suffered “a temporary collapse of his situational awareness.” Chung said the doctor, an experienced contract obstetrician-gynaecologist, admitted the mistake and apologised immediately, and that the hospital would take disciplinary action. He said the patient was shocked and disappointed but was still attending consultations with the doctor.

stories.headline: Xi tells APEC business leaders to defend free trade, then says China and Russia should “lead” a multipolar world
stories.deck: In a keynote to the APEC CEO Summit in Shenzhen on Wednesday, Xi Jinping called for upholding the WTO-centred trading system and pledged to lower tariffs and widen market access. After talks with Vladimir Putin, he said Beijing and Moscow should lead the move towards a multipolar world, Al Jazeera reported.
stories.summary: In a keynote to the APEC CEO Summit in Shenzhen on Wednesday, Xi Jinping called for upholding the WTO-centred trading system and pledged to lower tariffs and widen market access. After talks with Vladimir Putin, he said Beijing and Moscow should lead the move towards a multipolar world, Al Jazeera reported. “Stability brings security; security brings prosperity,” Xi said, according to RTHK, and he called for progress towards a Free Trade Area of the Asia-Pacific. Al Jazeera read his warnings about “unilateralism and protectionism” as veiled criticism of Donald Trump’s tariffs. In their meeting, Xi said China–Russia relations had stayed “as solid as a mountain,” and Putin said two-way trade had passed US$200 billion, RTHK reported; it was their fifth meeting this year. Speaking to the summit afterwards, Putin called Western powers “former hegemons” and said Europe was in a “humiliating decline,” according to Al Jazeera. Hong Kong leader John Lee said on Facebook that Xi’s speech had encouraged him and that Hong Kong could be a springboard for businesses entering the Greater Bay Area.
stories.why: Xi is presenting China as the steady defender of open trade on the eve of meeting Trump, while standing visibly beside Putin. That framing will shape how Asian governments and companies read Thursday’s three-way meeting, and whether they see Beijing or Washington as the more predictable partner.

stories.summary: A runway of nearly three kilometres is taking shape on Antelope Reef, which China has expanded from one of its smallest Paracel outposts into a large island in about 10 months, according to analysts and satellite images seen by AFP, as carried by Hong Kong Free Press. Reports by the Center for Strategic and International Studies and the Lowy Institute say large-scale dredging began late last year. The runway would be Beijing’s second in the Paracels, which are also claimed by Vietnam and Taiwan; China has controlled them since a 1974 clash with Vietnam. The Lowy report’s author, Lowell Bautista, said it helps “create an integrated network of runways, harbours and sensors stretching across the sea.” China says development in the Paracels is for civilian purposes; its foreign ministry said in March that land reclamation there was “necessary construction” to improve living and working conditions.
stories.why: A new airstrip lets China base aircraft further out over a sea that carries a large share of world shipping, and it comes days after Xi told Vietnam’s leader the two countries should manage their maritime differences. Neighbours and the U.S. will read it as a sign of how Beijing intends to back its claims.

stories.deck: Commission President Ursula von der Leyen on Wednesday proposed €45 billion in new support for Ukraine next year — €20 billion for the budget and €25 billion for weapons — to cover about two-thirds of what Brussels estimates is a €70 billion funding gap. stories.summary: Commission President Ursula von der Leyen on Wednesday proposed €45 billion in new support for Ukraine next year — €20 billion for the budget and €25 billion for weapons — to cover about two-thirds of what Brussels estimates is a €70 billion funding gap. It needs member states’ approval. “Ukraine only needs to repay once Russia pays for the damage it has caused,” she said, according to Interfax-Ukraine. Euronews reported the money would be raised through joint EU borrowing and would come on top of the €90 billion loan agreed last December; if Russia refuses to pay reparations, the EU reserves the right to use immobilised Russian assets. Von der Leyen said she was “very confident” all 27 members would back it; leaders are due to discuss it at a summit in Brussels. Separately, DW’s live coverage said Ukrainian media reported overnight drone strikes on two oil refineries in Russia’s Krasnodar region, a claim DW said it could not independently verify, a day after Ukraine’s strike on the Kerch bridge.
stories.why: Ukraine’s money for 2027 was the big open question in Europe; this proposal answers it if governments agree. Tying repayment to Russian reparations keeps pressure on Moscow as Putin sits down with Xi and Trump in Shenzhen.
